..
As of 355 PM Tuesday... 

KEY MESSAGE 1... An energetic pattern will favor coastal 
cyclogenesis that will offer cntl NC widespread rain, some possibly 
heavy, and gusty winds late Wed through at least early Thanksgiving 
Day. However, there remains uncertainty in the track of the coastal 
low (and related inland distribution of precipitation/amounts) and 
also mesoscale influences that may oppose the otherwise favorably-
forced, synoptic environment.  

A subtropical perturbation, now over the wrn Gulf and within an 
energetic srn stream, will progress across the Gulf and reach FL by 
around 12Z Wed, then pivot up the South Atlantic coast Wed and Wed 
night. The models indicate it will do so while slightly preceding a 
shortwave trough, now over the srn Plains, forecast to amplify 
considerably and assume negative tilt while pivoting across the nrn 
Gulf and Southeast, with standardized 500 mb negative height 
anomalies in excess of 5 sigma Wed-Wed night, then up the South and 
Middle Atlantic coasts Thu-Thu night. The models have also come into 
better agreement regarding some degree of phasing of that trough 
with a vigorous shortwave trough accompanying a cyclone forecast to 
dig sewd from the nrn Plains this afternoon to the Mid-South by 12Z 
Thu. That intense cyclone will then lift newd and across the OH 
Valley Thu-Thu night and nrn Middle Atlantic Fri. 

At the surface, an already strong, ~1036 mb cP high now over Lake MI 
is forecast to strengthen to between 1040-1045 mb while progressing 
across the Great Lakes and Northeast through early Wed night, before 
quickly weakening and retreating/progressing offshore through Thu. 
Meanwhile, multiple areas of pressure falls are expected to develop 
downstream of the mid/upr features noted above and along a couple 
of frontal zones draped from the Gulf to offshore the South Atlantic 
coast. There remains uncertainty regarding how quickly low pressure 
will consolidate from possibly as far south as the wrn tip of Cuba, 
to off the South Atlantic coast through early Wed night, and also to 
what degree inland of the srn Middle Atlantic coast (NC/VA) it may 
track later Wed night through Thu. 

The evolution of the low coastal low will have ramifications on both 
how quickly a related precipitation shield will mature and how far 
inland it will spread. The 12Z deterministic and ensemble guidance 
has generally trended slightly wwd/more inland with that track, with 
a resultant uptick in forecast precipitation totals into cntl NC 
(generally 2-3" - slightly lower wrn Piedmont and higher ern 
Piedmont and Coastal Plain). However, classical, diabatically 
enhanced cold air damming that will strengthen most strongly in the 
favored Piedmont/Foothills damming Wed into early Wed night, which 
NWP guidance typically erodes too quickly, may retard the inland 
retreat of the low more significantly than currently advertised by 
that guidance. Such a scenario would shift the footprint of the 
heaviest precipitation ewd, with lower totals across cntl NC. 
Regardless, a widespread, soaking rain is considered the most likely 
solution, with the strongest/deepest lift that will be centered upon 
Wed night, followed by abrupt drying aloft accompanying a mid-level 
dry slot punching in from the south and southwest during the day 
Thu. Although the arrival of that feature will cause the heaviest 
rain to shift north, lingering lower-level saturation would favor 
continued low overcast and periods of light rain/drizzle through at 
least early Thu night, before drier air arrives in wswly flow behind 
the departing low overnight. Although not depicted in NWP guidance, 
gravity waves often develop in such patterns and very near the 
leading edge of the dry air stream/dry slot, with further, rapid 
erosion of the back edge of the precipitation shield. 

Additionally, areas of convection already underway from the nrn Gulf 
to the Carolinas Gulf Stream Atlantic are forecast to grow in 
coverage and intensity as the mid/upr-level forcing noted above 
increases/overspreads the region. Although considered a less likely 
scenario, such developments will have the potential to alter the 
surrounding mass/flow fields and disrupt related advection and 
vertical motion fields that will be otherwise favorable for strong 
lift across cntl NC. REFS guidance in particular depicts such a 
scenario, with a significant QPF minimum inland of the coast and 
across cntl NC. 

The other forecast sensible weather, such as temperatures and 
diurnal changes within the CAD regime and also the potential for 
strong and gusty surface winds, otherwise remains unchanged from 
previous forecasts.
